# Ostrava Array

Site profile, revision 1.

The connection agreement limits export during summer evenings when the line is congested. Local councils asked for noise studies before approving the auxiliary cooling equipment. Operators report that availability improved after a firmware update to the inverters. Several neighbouring utilities have signed agreements to buy capacity during winter peaks. The developers published a lessons-learned report covering procurement and grid connection.

Maintenance crews inspect the containment and the power electronics on a quarterly schedule. Degradation is tracked with a monthly capacity test at a fixed state of charge. Grid operators value storage that can shift energy from midday surpluses to the evening peak. A second phase is under discussion, depending on the outcome of the next capacity auction. Commissioning tests ran for several weeks before the plant joined the balancing market.

The plant can black-start a nearby gas turbine, which the grid operator tests twice a year. The developers published a lessons-learned report covering procurement and grid connection. Round-trip efficiency is measured at the point of interconnection, after auxiliary loads. Spare parts are held on site to keep repair times short during the winter months. Analysts expect the levelized cost of storage to keep falling as supply chains mature.

## Key figures

- Technology: gravity storage

- Storage capacity: 931 MWh

- Round-trip efficiency: 63%

- Commissioned: 2030
